summary: Reserves the last Autonomous System Numbers in the 16-bit and 32-bit ranges and gives guidance on their use. It updates Section 10 of RFC 1930 and is a Best Current Practice.

eli5.summary: Numbers name networks. The very last numbers at the end of each range are set aside so they will not be given out by mistake.

questions: should last asns be filtered in bgp
subtitle: Explains why the last AS numbers of the 16-bit and 32-bit ranges are reserved and should not be used.

tldr.problem: The last AS numbers of each range, 65535 and 4294967295, border on the Private Use ranges, so operators might wrongly treat them as private.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC documents the reservation of both Last ASNs and tells operators not to use them or advertise them globally, while telling implementers not to treat their use as a protocol error.
tldr.outcome: The two numbers stay reserved: 65535 because of Well-known Communities, and 4294967295 as a candidate for a future Special Use ASN.

today: RFC 7300 is a Best Current Practice and has not been obsoleted. It updates RFC 1930.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: IANA reserved the last ASN of the 16-bit range, 65535, over a decade before this RFC. Since RFC 6793, IANA has also reserved the last ASN of the 32-bit range, 4294967295. Although these Last ASNs border on the Private Use ranges of RFC 6996, they are not reserved as Private Use ASNs. The RFC gives the reasoning and guidance for operators and implementers.
sections.eli5: The last number on each list is set aside, and it is not one of the free-to-use private numbers.

sections.title: Reasons for Reservation
sections.content: Some BGP communities of ASN 65535 are reserved for Well-known Communities, as described in RFC 1997. This is not currently true of 4294967295, but if a future Special Use ASN is needed that is not designed to be globally routable, that number could be a candidate. The document prescribes no such use at publication.
sections.eli5: One last number is already used for special messages, and the other is kept free in case a special job turns up.

sections.title: Guidance for Operators
sections.content: Operators SHOULD NOT use Last ASNs for any other purpose or as Private Use ASNs. For example, using AS 65535 as private might accidentally trigger BGP Well-known Community values and cause undesirable routing. Last ASNs MUST NOT be advertised to the global Internet within AS_PATH or AS4_PATH, and operators SHOULD filter them there.
sections.eli5: Do not use the reserved last number as your own, and do not let it leak out to the wider world.

sections.title: Guidance for Implementers
sections.content:
Last ASNs remain valid ASNs from a BGP perspective, so implementations SHOULD NOT treat their use as a protocol error. If a Last ASN is configured as the local AS, an implementation MAY warn about improper use of a reserved ASN. Tools that filter Private Use ASNs MAY also include Last ASNs.

On security, the RFC adds no new concerns, though BGP implementation errors could be triggered by Last ASN usage.
sections.eli5: Routers should not panic if they see the number, though they may politely warn.
